enumeration_note: One bidirectional Fibonacci pullback-continuation strategy; the buy and sell sides are mirror-image directional legs operating in mutually-exclusive trend contexts (not opposing strategies), captured as long/short variants.

coaching_notes: You always need to enter the market in early stages of its trend otherwise you'll end up losing your trade
You can't trade in a non trending market
if you'll follow each step carefully then the chances of loss are minimal
If you have identified the trend on its early stages then you can end up making huge profits from a single trend, because you just need to repeat the same process again and again
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: identify trend direction on the 4-hour timeframe using a trend line before taking any trade
PRECONDITION: only take buy trades when the market is in an uptrend; only take sell trades when the market is in a downtrend
Uses Fibonacci retracement indicator to identify entry levels
Buy entry: draw Fibonacci from swing low to recent swing high; enter anywhere between the 50% and 61.8% retracement levels when price touches them
Sell entry: draw Fibonacci from swing high to recent swing low; enter anywhere between the 50% and 61.8% retracement levels when price touches them
Buy take profit: above the previous swing high
Buy stop loss: below the swing low
Sell take profit: below the previous swing low
Sell stop loss: above the swing high
strategies.entry_summary: Trade pullbacks in the direction of the established trend. First identify trend direction on the 4-hour chart with a trend line; then on the 1-hour chart draw a Fibonacci retracement (swing low to recent swing high for uptrend / swing high to recent swing low for downtrend) and enter between the 50% and 61.8% retracement levels when price touches them. Buy only in an uptrend, sell only in a downtrend. Applies to any currency pair.
strategies.exit_summary: Buy: take profit above the previous swing high, stop loss below the swing low. Sell: take profit below the previous swing low, stop loss above the swing high.
